findings.description: The awk record is joined with the in-band separator US (0x1F) and split back with `IFS=$'\037' read`. The seventh field (the trailing `# comment` of the candidate `if:` line) is raw file content and may itself contain 0x1F, which shifts `norm` and `raw` by one or more fields. All earlier fields are awk-generated numerics or enums, so only the comment can shift. The fix path is protected solely because `_legacy_release_guard_rewrite` re-reads line N and compares it with the (now wrong) `raw`, which cannot match; the WARN-only path can be made to fire, or a genuine legacy guard with such a comment stays silent.
findings.failure_mode: When a workflow line is `    if: anything  #\x1f<legacy text>\x1f` then the detector reports the legacy guard on a non-legacy line and prints the legacy WARN; with LOA_SCAFFOLD_FIX_RELEASE_GUARD=1 the rewrite refuses with "line N changed since detection" instead of corrupting the file, so safety rests entirely on that compare staying in place.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or strip C0 control bytes (at least 0x1F) from the candidate line in the awk END block before emitting the record (print `notsingle` if present), or move the comment to the last position and length-prefix it; add a bats case with 0x1F in the trailing comment asserting silence and byte-identical output with and without the flag.
findings.failure_scenario: When a workflow line is `    if: anything  #\x1f<legacy text>\x1f` then the detector reports the legacy guard on a non-legacy line and prints the legacy WARN; with LOA_SCAFFOLD_FIX_RELEASE_GUARD=1 the rewrite refuses with "line N changed since detection" instead of corrupting the file, so safety rests entirely on that compare staying in place.

findings.description: The symlink refusal (`-L "$target"` at lines 67 and 167) covers only the final path component. `dirname` of the fixed relative target yields `.github/workflows`; if that directory or `.github` is a symlink committed in the repository being mounted, `mktemp "$dir/.post-merge.XXXXXX"` and `mv -f` operate inside the link target. The pre-existing fresh-install path (`mkdir -p` + `cp` / `git checkout`, lines 219-228) likewise creates `post-merge.yml` through the link. Impact is bounded: the rewrite needs legacy content already present at the destination, and the fresh path only creates a non-executable YAML file, so this is a hardening gap rather than an exploit.
findings.failure_mode: When a mounted repository ships `.github/workflows` as a symlink to a writable directory outside the working tree then the installer creates or rewrites `post-merge.yml` and a `.post-merge.XXXXXX` temp file in that directory instead of in the repository, and the "symlink refused" guarantee in the header comment does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Before writing, resolve `.github` and `.github/workflows` with lib/portable-realpath.sh and refuse (WARN, return 0) when either is a symlink or resolves outside `$PWD`; apply the same check ahead of `mkdir -p` in `scaffold_post_merge_workflow`. Add a bats case with `.github/workflows` as a symlink asserting no file is created outside the fixture repo.
findings.failure_scenario: When a mounted repository ships `.github/workflows` as a symlink to a writable directory outside the working tree then the installer creates or rewrites `post-merge.yml` and a `.post-merge.XXXXXX` temp file in that directory instead of in the repository, and the "symlink refused" guarantee in the header comment does not hold.

findings.cross_file_justification: Byte-budget enforcement and the degrade/merge-block decision live in core/paged-fetch.ts and core/truncation.ts (diff-touched); this test documents that protected paths are not exempt from the budget but does not pin the fail-closed consequence.
findings.description: The test establishes that a protected path (a workflow file kept despite an exclude pattern) can still be dropped by the byte budget and recorded as `byte_budget` / `reviewable: true`, but asserts nothing about `degraded`, `degraded_reasons` or `mergeBlockedReason` for that case. Protected paths are the control that stops workflow and hook changes from being hidden from review; a PR author controls both the byte volume and the listing order (GitHub lists files by path, so a large file under `.a/` precedes `.github/`). The `record()` fixture pairs `byte_budget` with `incomplete_coverage`, suggesting production blocks the merge, but no test pins that for a protected file.
findings.failure_mode: When a PR pairs a workflow edit with a budget-filling change in an earlier-sorted path then the workflow leaves the reviewed set; if the budget omission is not merge-blocking, or a later refactor stops it being so, the workflow change ships unreviewed and this suite stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: In this test assert `degraded === true`, `degraded_reasons` includes `incomplete_coverage` and `mergeBlockedReason === "incomplete_coverage"`. Consider having truncateFiles place protected-kept files ahead of the byte budget so they are cut last, with a test that a protected file survives when only non-protected files exceed the budget.
findings.failure_scenario: When a PR pairs a workflow edit with a budget-filling change in an earlier-sorted path then the workflow leaves the reviewed set; if the budget omission is not merge-blocking, or a later refactor stops it being so, the workflow change ships unreviewed and this suite stays green.
